primitives.name: Sleep State Transition Detector
primitives.verbatim_quote: In particular, a wearable, continuous physiological monitoring system as described herein includes one or more sensors to detect sleep states, the transitions between sleep states, and the transitions from a sleep state to an awake state for a user.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S(t)': 'Sleep state at time t, discrete {0,1,2,3} representing wake, light, deep, REM', 'T_{s\\to w}(t)': 'Time of transition from sleep to wake at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Sleep states follow Markovian dynamics; transitions occur at fixed intervals.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sensor data is corrupted or missing, S(t) becomes undefined.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to finite-state automaton with probabilistic transitions; GSE models state evolution via kernel-based temporal logic.
layer2.telemetry: Transition timestamps and state labels from sensor fusion.

primitives.name: Heart Rate Variability Calculator
primitives.verbatim_quote: This information can be used in conjunction with continuously monitored heart rate data to calculate heart rate variability of the user at the end of the last phase of sleep preceding the user waking up.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\sigma^2_{RR}(t)': 'Variance of RR-intervals at time t, ms²', 'RR_i': 'Individual RR interval, ms', '\\bar{RR}': 'Mean RR interval, ms'}
primitives.assumptions: RR intervals are stationary and normally distributed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When RR intervals exceed 2 seconds or fall below 200 ms, variance calculation fails.

layer2.mapping: Kernelized HRV estimator derived from time-series covariance; GSI infers recovery score via Bayesian posterior over HRV.
layer2.telemetry: RR-interval time series from ECG or PPG sensors.

primitives.name: Recovery Score Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: By using the history of heart rate data in conjunction with sleep activity in this manner, an accurate and consistent recovery score can be calculated based on heart rate variability.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R(t)': 'Recovery score at time t, dimensionless', '\\mu_{HRV}': 'Mean HRV value, ms²', '\\sigma^2_{HRV}': 'Variance of HRV, ms²', '\\mathcal{S}(S(t))': 'Sleep quality modifier function, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Recovery score is normally distributed around HRV mean weighted by sleep quality.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When HRV data is absent or inconsistent, R(t) becomes undefined.

layer2.mapping: Derived from HRV kernel with sleep-state weighting; GSE applies conformal prediction to recover score for adaptive training.
layer2.telemetry: Normalized recovery score from HRV and sleep state history.

The transition from sleep to wake (T_{s\to w}) acts as a boundary condition that triggers HRV computation. The HRV estimator computes variance of RR-intervals, which is a second-order moment of the interbeat interval distribution. This variance is then modulated by a sleep quality function S(t), yielding a scalar recovery score R(t). The system's failure mode occurs when either sensor data is missing or signal integrity degrades beyond acceptable thresholds. The dual nature of the model lies in its discrete-state evolution and continuous-time signal processing, forming a hybrid automaton. The epistemic closure is achieved through Bayesian updating of HRV parameters conditioned on observed sleep transitions.
